notes: Event date: 6 June 1944 (DANFS and Wikipedia: opened fire at 0537 from her station on the right flank of Utah Beach). Event definition: Quincy, in Task Group 125.8, opened fire at 0537 from a range of 16,000 yards on the right flank of Utah Beach (DANFS); she shot 42 8-inch shells at an enemy battery (DANFS). Event support: three source families (US Navy NHHC/DANFS, Wikipedia, Morison). Location: Utah Beach (place PL0357) with a precision of 25 km. Location support: DANFS and Wikipedia give the station (right flank of Utah Beach) and DANFS gives the range (16,000 yards, about 14.6 km) but no bearing; the flank is an area, so no sea point is worked, and the precision is opened to cover the stated range. Review: confidence 0.5 from the rubric (approximate sea position; the sector and a range are given, the bearing is not, so the beach stands for the operational area (0.5)); added in the Normandy chunk 1 pass (branch normandy-wtf-ships, 16 November 2026): old value none, new value this claim; parent_unit_id old value none, new value blank, reason: parents are left blank on claim rows (the chain is in the command relations). Senn (Battle Summary 39 App. B(1) "Elliott Senn"; DANFS "Elliot M. Senn"; Morison App. I "E. M. Senn").

notes: Event date: 25 June 1944 (Quincy DANFS: sailed from Portland at 0508 on the 25th in Group 1; caption of shells off her bow, 25 June; returned to Portland at 1931 that evening). Wikipedia says she departed Portland on 24 June for Cherbourg: Quincy DANFS has a 24 June conference and a counter-march back to the anchorage, with the attack set for the following day, so the 24 June Wikipedia date is the eve of the operation, not a competing bombardment date. Event definition: Quincy, in Group 1 of Task Force 129, took part in the bombardment of Cherbourg (DANFS, Morison). Event support: three source families (US Navy NHHC/DANFS, Wikipedia, Morison). Location: Offshore Cherbourg, 12,000 yards north (Fire Support Area 1, place PL4182) with a precision of 5 km. Location support: Nevada DANFS gives this as the group noon position on 25 June and names Quincy in the group. Review: confidence 0.5 from the rubric (approximate sea position from a stated range and direction for the group, sea_position cap (0.5)); added in the Normandy chunk 1 pass (branch normandy-wtf-ships, 16 November 2026): old value none, new value this claim; parent_unit_id old value none, new value blank, reason: parents are left blank on claim rows (the chain is in the command relations). Context: Old value none, new value the group sea point, reason: Nevada DANFS states the group position and names Quincy. Quincy DANFS calls the sailing "TG 125.1"; the group is stored as US-TG-129-1 (decision D6). The group number is secondary. Wikipedia "24 June" departure is explained in the event date, not entered as a competing claim.
